name: Fuse & Polyfuse Selector
blurb: fuse rating from normal current and fault scenario
intro: A fuse rating from the normal current (75 % derating, re-rated for temperature), checked against the inrush pulse's I²t and against the fault current that has to blow it. Method: Littelfuse Fuseology selection guide; PTCs sized on hold current at temperature.

inputs.label: Normal operating current
inputs.help: The highest steady current in normal use (RMS).

inputs.label: Circuit voltage
inputs.help: The highest open-circuit voltage the fuse can see once blown.

inputs.label: Inrush duration (τ for exponential)
inputs.help: For a capacitor charge: τ = R·C of the charging path.

inputs.label: Fault current available
inputs.help: What the source can push into a short: supply current limit, battery short-circuit current.

examples.title: 12 V input, 1.5 A load, 100 µF bulk capacitor

usage: Give the fuse type (fast, slow or ptc), the normal current in A, circuit voltage in V, ambient temperature in °C, the inrush pulse (shape, peak A, duration ms, number of pulses) and the fault current in A. It returns the minimum rating and the next standard rating (hold current for a PTC), the inrush I²t and the melting I²t the fuse must have, the voltage and breaking-capacity it must be rated for, and whether the fault is big enough to open it quickly. Use it when choosing an input or port fuse.
sources: Littelfuse Fuseology Selection Guide (75 % operating-current derating, temperature re-rating, pulse I²t factors 38/29/22 % for 1k/10k/100k pulses)
UL 248-14 opening times (135 % within 60 min, 200 % within 2 min)
PTC hold-current derating: typical PPTC datasheet curves (Littelfuse, Bourns), approximated linearly
